feedback.problem:
Let ${J}_{n}(\lambda )$ denote an $n\times n$ Jordan block with $\lambda $ on the main diagonal. Fill in the missing entries in the matrix below.

|  |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} | {{field-3}} | $0$ |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${({J}_{3}(2)\,⊕\,{J}_{1}(3))}^{4}=\,\,$ |  | $0$ | $16$ | {{field-4}} | $0$ |  |
|  | $0$ | $0$ | $16$ | $0$ |  |  |
|  |  | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ | {{field-5}} |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
Given a function $f$ and a Jordan block ${J}_{n}(\lambda ),$ we have

$$
f({J}_{n}(\lambda ))=[\begin{aligned}f(\lambda ) & {f}^{′}(\lambda ) & \frac{{f}^{″}(\lambda )}{2!} & ⋯ & \frac{{f}^{(n-1)}(\lambda )}{(n-1)!} \\ 0 & f(\lambda ) & {f}^{′}(\lambda ) & ⋯ & \frac{{f}^{(n-2)}(\lambda )}{(n-2)!} \\ ⋮ & ⋱ & ⋱ & ⋱ & ⋮ \\ 0 & ⋯ & 0 & f(\lambda ) & {f}^{′}(\lambda ) \\ 0 & ⋯ & ⋯ & 0 & f(\lambda )\end{aligned}].
$$

First, note that

$$
\begin{aligned}{({J}_{3}(2)\,⊕\,{J}_{1}(3))}^{4} & ={([\begin{aligned}{J}_{3}(2) & 0 \\ 0 & {J}_{1}(3)\end{aligned}])}^{4} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{({J}_{3}(2))}^{4} & 0 \\ 0 & {({J}_{1}(3))}^{4}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={({J}_{3}(2))}^{4}\,⊕\,{({J}_{1}(3))}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we compute the function of each Jordan block separately.

- For ${J}_{3}(2),$ we have $n=3$ and $\lambda =2.$ \since $n=3,$ we need to compute the first and second derivatives of $f$ only:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={x}^{4} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =4{x}^{3} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =12{x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f({J}_{3}(2)) & =[\begin{aligned}f(2) & {f}^{′}(2) & \frac{{f}^{″}(2)}{2} \\ 0 & f(2) & {f}^{′}(2) \\ 0 & 0 & f(2)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{2}^{4} & 4\cdot {2}^{3} & \frac{12\cdot {2}^{2}}{2} \\ 0 & {2}^{4} & 4\cdot {2}^{3} \\ 0 & 0 & {2}^{4}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}16 & 32 & 24 \\ 0 & 16 & 32 \\ 0 & 0 & 16\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

- For ${J}_{1}(3),$ we have $n=1$ and $\lambda =1.$ since $n=1,$ we don't need any derivatives. So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f({J}_{1}(3)) & =[\begin{aligned}f(3)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{3}^{4}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}81\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{({J}_{3}(2)\,⊕\,{J}_{1}(3))}^{4} & ={({J}_{3}(2))}^{4}\,⊕\,{({J}_{1}(3))}^{4} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}16 & 32 & 24 & 0 \\ 0 & 16 & 32 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 16 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 81\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
